events.what: Fox, Pach and Suk prove the conjecture for large k when the graph has at most 1.4(k-1) vertices
Cranston proves the conjecture for r<=24
Sadhu v1 claims the conjecture for r<=26
events.credibility_reason: Same author and manuscript later ballooned to an all-r claim within twelve days; the r<=26 part is used by Cao & Mehat but not independently checked.

events.what: Sadhu v2 claims a full proof for every r
events.credibility_reason: F5: scope jump from r<=26 to all r in twelve days on a problem where full resolution would be a landmark; solo author; only automated (Pith) review; the concurrent Cao-Mehat r<=29 paper does not engage the all-r claim; method mixes certificate verification with an asymptotic regime that the prior literature only reached for restricted vertex counts.
events.ai_basis: ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used for literature-search, language-editing, and verification assistance.

events.what: Cao and Mehat prove the conjecture for r<=29, building on Cranston and Sadhu v1
events.ai_basis: generative AI/LLMs were used 'substantially' for 'mathematical exploration, intermediate checking, and manuscript drafting'

events.what: ProofAtlas AI-agent workspace reports unaudited exclusions for r>=5442

judgement.doubts: Sadhu v2 is set aside as not_credible chiefly on the scope-ballooning signal; it is only weeks old, so the no-uptake signal is weak. If a named expert endorses it, status becomes resolved. Cao-Mehat's 'mathematical exploration' LLM use could hide AI-produced content, but no specific piece is attributed to AI, so kept none. The r<=29 result partly relies on Sadhu v1's r<=26 step.

outcome_prefix: Judged: status rests on Cao & Mehat's September 2026 preprint proving Albertson's conjecture for chromatic number r<=29; Sadhu's all-r v2 claim is set aside as not credible.
